'''Adem Bona''' (born '''Ikechukwu Stanley Okoro'''; 28 March 2003) is a Nigerian-Turkish [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. Named a [[McDonald's All-American]] in high school, he was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team and voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]] in 2023. Bona was a first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] selection and voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]] in 2024.

==Early life and career==
Bona was born Ikechukwu Stanley Okoro in [[Lagos]], Nigeria, as the youngest of five children.<ref name="abcspor">{{cite web |title=Adem Bona kimdir? |url=https://abcspor.com/adem-bona-kimdir/ |publisher=ABCSpor |accessdate=4 April 2020 |language=Turkish |date=5 August 2019}}</ref> He grew up playing [[association football]] as a [[midfielder]] but switched to [[basketball]] due to his height.<ref name="fiba">{{cite web |title=Finally playing with same age, Bona takes leadership role in quest for podium top step |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2019/news/finally-playing-with-same-age-bona-takes-leadership-role-in-quest-for-podium-top-step |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=4 April 2020 |date=13 August 2019}}</ref> He often played basketball with makeshift hoops in fields, sometimes without a ball. Okoro was playing for about one year when a video of him drew the attention of Turkish coach Türkay Çakıroğlu, who then contacted Istanbul Basket coach Nevzat Özdemir.<ref name="arioz">{{cite web |last=Arıöz |first=Levent |title=Yeni Bobby Adem |url=https://www.dokuzeylul.com/spor/yeni-bobby-adem-h148848.html |website=9 Eylül Gazetesi |accessdate=4 April 2020 |language=Turkish |date=9 March 2019}}</ref> At age 13, Bona moved to Turkey, leaving behind the rest of his family, and began his career with Istanbul Basket.<ref name=fiba/><ref name="trt">{{cite web |title=Karşınızda Adem Bona |url=https://www.trtspor.com.tr/haber/detay/karsinizda-adem-bona-189722.html |publisher=TRT Spor |accessdate=4 April 2020 |language=Turkish |date=18 August 2019}}</ref> In February 2019, he moved to [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]] and continued competing at the youth level.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adem Bona'yı Pınar Karşıyaka Kaptı! |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/tr/tbl-tr/822571/adem-bonayi-pinar-karsiyaka-kapti-foto/ |publisher=Eurohoops |accessdate=4 April 2020 |language=Turkish |date=3 February 2019}}</ref>

On 30 October 2019, Bona made his professional debut for Pınar Karşıyaka, playing one minute in a 77–57 win over [[Donar (basketball club)|Donar]] in the [[FIBA Europe Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pınar Karşıyaka, Groningen'e fark attı! 16 yaşındaki Adem Bona ilk kez... |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/pinar-karsiyaka-groningene-fark-atti-16-yasindaki-adem-bona-ilk-kez-41363518 |website=[[Hürriyet]] |accessdate=4 April 2020 |language=Turkish |date=31 October 2019}}</ref> On 16 November, he debuted in the [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL), scoring two points in an 84–55 victory over [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Adem Bona: "Gösterdikleri Destekten Ötürü Taraftarlarımıza Teşekkür Ediyorum" |url=https://kskbasketbol.net/2019/11/16/adem-bona-gosterdikleri-destekten-oturu-taraftarlarimiza-tesekkur-ediyorum/ |publisher=[[Karşıyaka Basket]] |accessdate=4 April 2020 |language=Turkish |date=16 November 2019}}</ref>

==High school career==
On 18 September 2020, it was announced that Bona would continue his career at Prolific Prep in [[Napa, California]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Robledillo |first=Albert |title=Adem Bona ('03) chooses USA over Europe |url=http://www.eurohopes.com/news/6307/adem_bona_03_chooses_usa_over_europe |publisher=Eurohopes |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=18 September 2020}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Bona is a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. On 1 November 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] over an offer from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].

==College career==
As a [[freshman]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], in [[2022–23 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2022–23]], Bona improved after about a month of [[foul trouble]] and dropped passes.<ref name=bolch_01192023>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Making everywhere he goes his happy place, Adem Bona is a rising star for UCLA|date=19 January 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-01-19/adem-bona-ucla-basketball-nigeria-nba-potential-mick-cronin|access-date=20 January 2023}}</ref> On 2 January 2023, he was named the [[Pac-12]]'s freshman of the week after scoring the go-ahead basket in a comeback win over [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], followed by a season-high 18 points and three [[block (basketball)|blocks]] in a victory against [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].<ref name=bolch_01192023/><ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Adem Bona takes charge for No. 11 UCLA in blowout win over Washington|date=1 January 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-01-01/ucla-washington-pac-12-basketball-game-recap|access-date=22 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Pac-12 Men's Basketball Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva - January 2, 2023|date=2 January 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/01/02/pac-12-mens-basketball-performance-awards-presented-nextiva-january-2-2023|access-date=22 January 2023}}</ref> He won consecutive freshman of the week honors after grabbing 10 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] along with two blocked shots to help UCLA beat [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].<ref name=bolch_01192023/><ref>{{cite web|title=Pac-12 Men's Basketball Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva - January 9, 2023|date=9 January 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/01/09/pac-12-mens-basketball-performance-awards-presented-nextiva-january-9-2023|access-date=22 January 2023}}</ref> On 2 March, Bona had a career-high 11 rebounds against [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Adem Bona|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/adem-bona/11950|access-date=10 November 2023}}</ref> In the [[2023 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2023 Pac-12 tournament]], he injured his left shoulder in the semifinals against [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Grosbard|title=Undersized UCLA loses thrilling Pac-12 Tournament title game to Arizona|date=11 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/11/undersized-ucla-loses-thrilling-pac-12-championship-game-to-arizona/|access-date=12 March 2023}}</ref> He missed the finals against [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], who defeated UCLA for the title.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA falls to Arizona in Pac-12 title game, hurting chances for a No. 1 NCAA seed|date=11 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-11/ucla-mens-basketball-loses-to-arizona-pac-12-recap|access-date=12 March 2023}}</ref>

The Bruins received a No. 2 seed in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]]. Bona was cleared to return in their opener, but he did not play in the 86–53 blowout over No. 15 seed [[UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball|UNC Asheville]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA dodges upset trend, opens NCAA tournament with rout of UNC Asheville|date=16 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-16/ucla-vs-unc-asheville-ncaa-tournament-recap|access-date=18 March 2023}}</ref> He returned in the following game against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], but reaggravated his shoulder during the game late in the game. He was out for two minutes before returning to make a key block in the final minutes to help secure a 68–63 win over the seventh-seeded Wildcats.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dylan|last=Hernandez|title=Don’t fret about UCLA. Resilience is part of the Bruins’ March Madness style|date=18 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-18/ucla-basketball-northwestern-adversity-title|access-date=20 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA edges Northwestern to advance to 3rd straight Sweet Sixteen|date=18 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/18/ucla-edges-northwestern-to-advance-to-third-straight-sweet-sixteen/|access-date=20 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA will need new strategy for Drew Timme if Adem Bona, David Singleton out vs. Gonzaga|date=21 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-21/ucla-bruins-basketball-injuries-sweet-16-gonzaga-drew-timme-ncaa-tournament|access-date=24 March 2023}}</ref> He was sidelined again for their next game against [[2022–23 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]], which UCLA lost 79–76.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jubilation turns into heartbreak as UCLA loses to Gonzaga again in NCAA tournament|date=23 March 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-23/ucla-basketball-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament-sweet-16-recap|access-date=24 March 2023}}</ref> For the season, Bona [[starting lineup|started]] 32 games and averaged 7.7 points and 5.3 rebounds in 22.9 minutes per game,<ref name=ocregister_05312023/> and led the Bruins with 57 blocks.<ref name=bolch_04192023/> He converted 67.5% of his [[field goal (basketball)|field goals]], which ranked second in the Pac-12.<ref name=bolch_04192023>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA’s Adem Bona declares for NBA draft but will preserve college eligibility|date=19 April 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-04-19/ucla-adem-bona-declares-for-nba-draft-preserve-college-eligibility|access-date=8 May 2023}}</ref> He was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive and Pac-12 All-Freshman teams and was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]]. He also received honorable mention for the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] team.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|date=7 March 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/03/07/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance|access-date=7 March 2023}}</ref> After the season, he [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] for the [[2023 NBA draft]], while retaining his college eligibility.<ref name=bolch_04192023/> Following surgery for a torn [[glenoid labrum|labrum]] in April, which prevented him from engaging in individual workouts prior to the draft, Bona withdrew from the draft.<ref name=ocregister_05312023>{{cite web|title=UCLA’s Adem Bona returning, Jaylen Clark remains in NBA draft|date=31 May 2023|work=The Orange County Register|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/05/31/uclas-adem-bona-returning-jaylen-clark-remains-in-nba-draft/|access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref>

While recovering from his injury, Bona added a midrange [[jump shot (basketball)|jump shot]] and [[post up|post]] moves to his offensive game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Stopping the biggest UCLA team of the Mick Cronin era could be a tall order|date=6 November 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-11-06/ucla-basketball-preview-bruins-tall-order|access-date=10 November 2023}}</ref> He did not play in the Bruins' tour of Spain or in their exhibition game. In their [[2023–24 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2023–24]] season opener, he had career-highs of 28 points and four blocks in a 75–44 win over [[Saint Francis Red Flash men's basketball|Saint Francis]]. He also had nine rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Adem Bona lives up to his billing as UCLA’s best player in season-opening win|date=10 November 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-11-06/ucla-mens-basketball-season-opener-saint-francis|access-date=10 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=John|last=Davis|title=UCLA routs St. Francis in season opener to give Mick Cronin a milestone win|date=6 November 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/11/06/ucla-routs-st-francis-in-season-opener-to-give-mick-cronin-a-milestone-win/|access-date=11 November 2023}}</ref> Bona was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team and voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]], the second consecutive Bruin to win the award after [[Jaylen Clark]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Keeping it in the UCLA family, Adem Bona wins Pac-12 defensive player of the year|date=12 March 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-03-12/pac-12-awards|access-date=14 March 2024}}</ref> He averaged 12.4 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game, but continued to get into foul trouble. After the season, Bona announced that he was leaving UCLA and declaring for the [[2024 NBA draft]]. He finished with 115 career blocks, which ranked sixth in Bruins' history.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA’s Adem Bona declares for NBA draft and bids farewell after two seasons|date=12 April 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-04-12/ucla-adem-bona-declares-nba-draft|access-date=13 April 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
At the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Udine]], Bona averaged 14.1 points, 10.3 rebounds, and four blocks per game, leading [[Turkey national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Turkey]] to fifth place. He ranked second at the tournament in rebounds and blocks and was named to the All-Star Five.<ref>{{cite web |title=MVP Dominguez headlines All-Star Five in Udine |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2019/news/mvp-dominguez-headlines-all-star-five-in-udine |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=4 April 2020 |date=17 August 2019}}</ref>
